task.description:
WF-03 Step 5 -- CLOSE OUT ISS-0109's RECORD. You diagnosed this issue at Step 1 of this same
run; this step makes the registry tell the truth about what was found and what shipped.

ORCH HAS ALREADY DECIDED THE STATUS, and it is deliberately NOT `resolved`. Both the
gate-approved design (SS8.3) and REVIEWER independently concluded this run is INSTRUMENTED, NOT
FIXED: no production defect exists to remove, the failure was never reproduced on demand, and
the root cause is still unknown. Marking it `resolved` would put a false entry into a registry
that six other issues cross-reference. Set:

    status: instrumented
    superseded_by: ISS-0116

WHAT YOU MUST DO:

1. CORRECT THE `mechanism:` SECTION. This is the MAJOR finding you yourself filed at Step 1 and
   it is the single most important edit in this step -- the record currently asserts a causal
   ordering its own evidence does not support, and any future run reading it would be misled
   exactly as this one nearly was. Rewrite it to state: the DROP/DELETE/DELETE triple is the
   failing test's OWN post-failure on_exit teardown (a consequence, not the cause), on the three
   grounds you established (schema_name_for_tenant/1 is a pure derivation so only the failing
   test's own closure can name that schema; ExUnit runs on_exit synchronously between tests and
   kills an over-running runner; the DROP used IF EXISTS and SUCCEEDED); that the only
   untimestamped line in the original excerpt was the one asserting causal order; and that
   failure 14's state (a table missing while its schema survived AND a sibling table in that
   schema was writable) is one DROP SCHEMA ... CASCADE physically cannot produce. PRESERVE the
   original text rather than deleting it -- keep it under a clearly marked heading such as
   `mechanism_as_originally_filed:` so the audit trail of what was believed, and when, survives.
   That is this project's convention (see the record's own `renumbered_from`/`renumber_note`
   handling) and it is what lets a later reader see the correction rather than a silent rewrite.

2. EXTEND `related:` with ISS-0107 and ISS-0059 (Step 0.5's finding), plus this run's own
   filings: ISS-0110, ISS-0111, ISS-0112, ISS-0113, ISS-0114, ISS-0115, ISS-0116.

3. RECORD WHAT SHIPPED and what it does and does not close. Add a resolution/outcome section
   naming: test/support/tenant_fixture.ex (Letflow.TenantFixture -- capture_schema_state/1's
   14-field one-shot report, assert_schema_complete!/2's completeness oracle, and the
   LETFLOW_TENANT_FIXTURE teardown marker with its closed phase vocabulary), its adoption in the
   two modules this issue names, the 14 regression tests at
   test/letflow/support/tenant_fixture_test.exs, the spec at test/specs/ISS-0109.md, and the
   design at lib/letflow/design/iss0109-provisioning-completeness-and-fixture-instrumentation.md.
   State plainly that this makes a recurrence ATTRIBUTABLE rather than making it stop happening.

4. ADD THE NEW EVIDENCE FROM THIS RUN'S OWN FULL SUITE, which is the most important new fact in
   the record and the reason ISS-0116 exists. TEST-RUNNER's run (612.1s, 1228/1244 passed, 16
   failures, seed 993324) produced a SIGNATURE-IDENTICAL reproduction of this issue's failure 3
   -- same 3F000, same {:error, {:migration_failed, %MatchError{...}}} wrapper, same failing
   assertion -- in Letflow.Definitions.RollbackTest (test/letflow/definitions/rollback_test.exs:642,
   raised from that module's own hand-rolled provisioned_tenant/0 at :120), a module that has NOT
   adopted the new fixture. Meanwhile BOTH modules this issue names passed, in the full suite and
   in isolation. Record it with the honesty TEST-RUNNER used: one observation, not a controlled
   experiment -- but evidence the condition is real and not specific to the two modules this
   issue happened to name. Full details: test/reports/report-20260821-WF03-ISS0109-20260821.yaml.

5. GITHUB. Post a comment on issue #358 and then CLOSE it deliberately (`gh issue comment` then
   `gh issue close`), rather than leaving it for the queue's release to close as a side effect.
   The comment must say: what shipped; that the originally-filed mechanism was refuted and how;
   that the root cause remains UNKNOWN so this is instrumented rather than fixed; that the
   remaining hunt now lives in ISS-0116/GH#370 WITH the new RollbackTest evidence; and that
   ISS-0112/GH#366 (adopting the fixture at the remaining sites) should be sequenced first
   because it is what makes the next occurrence diagnosable. Link #370 explicitly. If `gh` is
   unavailable, say so explicitly in your result rather than silently skipping -- do not fake it.

DO NOT: change any code, test, or the design artefact. Do not re-run the suite. This step edits
the issue registry and GitHub only.

CONSTRAINTS: timestamps from the clock (`date -u +"%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ"`), never estimated. Never
delete an issue file. Branch feature/WF03-ISS0109-20260821; commit by explicit filename, never `git add -A`.
handoffs/orchestrator.log is ORCH's -- leave it alone, and `git fetch` rather than pulling if a
rebase refuses.
acceptance_criteria: docs/issues/ISS-0109.yaml carries status: instrumented and superseded_by: ISS-0116 -- NOT status: resolved
The mechanism: section is corrected to the refutation established at Step 1, and the originally-filed text is PRESERVED under a clearly marked heading rather than deleted
related: is extended with ISS-0059, ISS-0107, ISS-0110, ISS-0111, ISS-0112, ISS-0113, ISS-0114, ISS-0115 and ISS-0116
A resolution/outcome section names every artefact that shipped and states plainly that this makes a recurrence attributable rather than making it stop happening

The RollbackTest reproduction from this run's full suite is recorded, with its file:line, the error signature, the fact that the two adopted modules passed, and the explicit caveat that it is one observation rather than a controlled experiment

GitHub issue #358 has a comment covering what shipped, the refuted mechanism, the unknown root cause, and the handoff to ISS-0116/GH#370 and ISS-0112/GH#366 -- and is then closed deliberately; or gh unavailability is stated explicitly
resolved_in_run / closed timestamps come from a real clock read
No code, test, spec or design file was modified by this step
